subject: AWS Marketplace metering preflight & procurement questions
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebio.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmebio.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on AWS Marketplace metering + entitlement flow for Redwood SaaS

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the predictable latency and the routing options. Our procurement and billing teams had a few practical questions before we move to internal approvals. Can you confirm the following?

1) Entitlement model: we want firm mapping from Marketplace product codes to our SaaS user accounts. Does Redwood provide a mapping file or webhook that we can use to reconcile usage claims to our internal account IDs?

2) Metering granularity: we plan to meter by active seats per hour. Can we send custom usage dimensions (e.g., seat-tier, feature-flag) as part of the metering payload, and how are those reported in settlement files?

3) Contract & invoicing: will Redwood accept Marketplace fulfillment (AWS SaaS) with Redwood appearing as the seller? We need clarity on who issues invoices to AcmeBio and whether we receive a consolidated monthly CSV for our own internal chargeback.

4) Proof points for procurement: for SOC2 and data residency, procurement wants a short list of evidence items we can attach to the purchase order. Can you send a one-page checklist?

I'll drop in the procurement team on reply. Ideally we get these answers by end of next week so legal can line up internal reviewers.

Thanks,
Alice Morgan
Director, IT Procurement
AcmeBio, Inc.

Attachment(s): none

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebio.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmebio.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on AWS Marketplace metering + entitlement flow for Redwood SaaS

Thanks Alice — looping in Dylan (SE) and Marissa (Marketplace ops) to confirm implementation details. High-level answers below, will follow up with a short matrix and attachments (entitlement mapping template + short SOC2 evidence checklist).

- Entitlement mapping: Redwood supports an entitlement webhook and periodic CSV reconciliation. We can also supply an entitlement_map_v1.xlsx template that maps AWS product code -> Redwood product_id -> customer_account_id (your internal id). That file can be used during onboarding and for backfills.

- Metering dimensions: Yes — the AWS MeterUsage API allows custom usage dimensions. For SaaS metering we recommend a primary dimension of seat-hours and a secondary dimension for "tier" so settlement rows include both. Our fulfillment connector aggregates to daily settlement CSVs with dimension columns preserved.

- Contract & invoicing: For AWS SaaS fulfillment, Redwood acts as the seller of record when using the Managed SaaS Seller flow. AWS will invoice AcmeBio (depending on your Marketplace preferences) and provide reports; Redwood can also provide a consolidated monthly CSV that shows AWS charges and the Redwood-side allocation for your internal chargeback. We'll include sample invoice fragments in the attachment.

- SOC2 / evidence: we'll send a 1-page checklist with links to SOC2 summary, encryption/KMS notes, and an export of audit-log retention policy. Note: full reports need an NDA / SOC2 request process.

I'll attach the entitlement mapping template and draft SOW for procurement to review. If that's good, I'll prepare a short mutual action plan and a DocuSign envelope for the Marketplace contract.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): entitlement_map_v1.xlsx, SaaS_SOW_draft.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebio.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmebio.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on AWS Marketplace metering + entitlement flow for Redwood SaaS

Irene / Marissa,

Quick tech notes for Alice so procurement understands integration constraints:

- Metering payload: Redwood's collector accepts a JSON payload with fields: customer_id, timestamp, dimension_map (key/value), usage_quantity. We sign requests with a per-customer API key. If Acme wants to push seat-hours, best practice is a periodic batch (hourly) rather than one event per seat to reduce API rate limits.

- Entitlement reconciliation: we expose a GET /entitlements endpoint for your internal systems to pull current active entitlements (product_code -> account_id -> effective_date). For reconciliations we support daily mismatch reports and a reconciliation API to submit correction deltas.

- Edge cases: if customers use multiple accounts / sub-orgs, include an external_id in the mapping to preserve your internal hierarchies — the entitlement_map_v1.xlsx has a column for that.

I'll also attach a one-page "Billing artifact sample" that shows the settlement CSV columns and a sample row.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your billing team tomorrow afternoon to walk the sample.

—Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): billing_artifact_sample.csv

Subject: Re: Questions on AWS Marketplace metering + entitlement flow for Redwood SaaS

Alice / Procurement team — thanks for the questions and patience. Quick summary and next steps:

1) Deliverables attached: entitlement_map_v1.xlsx (template), SaaS_SOW_draft.pdf (commercial + fulfillment notes), billing_artifact_sample.csv, and a 1-page SOC2 evidence checklist (inline below).

2) Confirmation: Redwood supports push metering (signed API key) or a partner-pull model — we can enable whichever you prefer. Settlement CSV will preserve custom dimensions and provide daily aggregates.

3) Invoicing / seller of record: Redwood will be the seller under the Managed SaaS Seller flow. AWS issues the charges to AcmeBio (per the Marketplace settings) and we provide the consolidated reconciliation CSV for your internal use.

4) SOC2 brief (for PO):
- SOC2 Type II: summary available upon request and under an NDA
- Data encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, KMS integration for customer-controlled keys (Private deployments)
- Audit logs: 365-day retention for hosted accounts (longer for enterprise add-on)
- Access controls: SSO (SAML/OIDC) + role-based access; exportable access reports

Next steps I propose:
- You review SOW and mapping template (attached).
- If OK, we prepare a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a DocuSign for the Marketplace fulfillment agreement.
- Dylan available for a 30-min billing walkthrough Wednesday 11am PT — shall I invite?

If you'd like me to prepare a one-page summary for Legal / PO with the key contract bullets, say the word and I’ll send it.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): entitlement_map_v1.xlsx, SaaS_SOW_draft.pdf, billing_artifact_sample.csv, soc2_checklist_onepager.pdf
